original_question: How do G2-instantons on the Bogoyavlenskaya family of G2-manifolds behave as the underlying metric is deformed by changing the asymptotic circle size? In the large-circle limit, do these instantons converge to G2-instantons for the Bryant-Salamon metric on R^4 x S^3, and in the small-circle limit, what precise relation do they have to Calabi-Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold?
target_in_paper: Section 4.4, open problem (e): the ALC open problem asking for the behavior of G2-instantons on the Bogoyavlenskaya family as the asymptotic circle size varies, with an expected Bryant–Salamon limit for large circle size and only a possible relation to Calabi–Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold for small circle size. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the Bogoyavlenskaya family on R^4 × S^3, the deformation by the ALC circle size at infinity, and the two asymptotic regimes singled out in the paper: a large-circle regime expected to resemble Bryant–Salamon G2-instantons, and a small-circle regime expected to have some relation to Calabi–Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
missing_details: The paper presents this as an open problem in the ALC section, not as a theorem or formal conjecture. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The metric family should be identified more precisely as the 1-parameter family, up to overall scaling, of SU(2)^2 × U(1)-invariant cohomogeneity-1 holonomy-G2 metrics on R^4 × S^3 constructed by Bogoyavlenskaya. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The phrase 'asymptotic circle size' is encoded in the ALC model by the parameter m in g_{ϕ∞} = dr^2 + m^2 η∞^2 + r^2 π^*g5. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The paper’s nearby context also notes that in the Bogoyavlenskaya family one can vary independently the circle size at infinity and the size of the associative S^3, and that the Bryant–Salamon metric appears as a limit of this family. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The scope is the invariant/cohomogeneity-1 instanton setting studied in Section 4, not arbitrary G2-instantons on arbitrary deformations. The section introduction explicitly says the constructions on the BGGG metric extend to the whole Bogoyavlenskaya family. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The draft makes the small-circle statement too strong: the paper says only that there may be a relation with Calabi–Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold, not that a precise relation is already expected in a fixed formal sense. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

The nearby precise mechanism connecting ALC G2-instantons to Calabi–Yau monopoles is Proposition 9: if a G2-instanton has a U(1)-invariant asymptotic model A∞ = a + mΦ ⊗ η∞ at infinity, then (a, Φ) is a Calabi–Yau monopole on the asymptotic Calabi–Yau cone. Your draft does not distinguish this cone-level statement from the more speculative deformed-conifold statement in open problem (e). ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify the underlying manifold R^4 × S^3 and indicate that the asymptotic cone in this setting comes from the Sasaki–Einstein structure on S^2 × S^3. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
refined_question: For the 1-parameter (up to overall scale) Bogoyavlenskaya family of complete SU(2)^2 × U(1)-invariant holonomy-G2 metrics on R^4 × S^3, whose ALC end has circle-size parameter m and which includes the BGGG metric and has the Bryant–Salamon metric as a limit, determine how the G2-instantons known on this family behave as m varies: in the large-circle regime m → ∞, do they limit to G2-instantons for the Bryant–Salamon metric on R^4 × S^3, and in the small-circle regime m → 0, is there a limiting relation between these G2-instantons and Calabi–Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold?
justification: The draft is essentially a sharpened paraphrase of Section 4.4(e), which is the only place in the paper that simultaneously mentions deformation of Bogoyavlenskaya G2-instantons by the circle size at infinity, an expected Bryant–Salamon behavior when that circle becomes large, and a possible relation to Calabi–Yau monopoles on the deformed conifold when it becomes small. The meaning of 'circle size at infinity' comes from the ALC model introduced at the start of Section 4.1, where the asymptotic metric has the form dr^2 + m^2η∞^2 + r^2π^*g5, and Proposition 9 provides the paper’s precise nearby statement relating asymptotic ALC G2-instantons to Calabi–Yau monopoles. The family-level context that the Bryant–Salamon metric arises as a limit of Bogoyavlenskaya metrics appears in Section 4.3.1. ([discovery.ucl.ac.uk](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10067480/1/1812.11867v1.pdf))
